title: Palisade retail ops onramp notebook
content:
Call: Palisade Retail Ops — 2026-02-17 11:00 PT (initial technical intake)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood CS), Hiro (Solutions Eng), Leah (Account Exec), Palisade: Simone (CTO), Raj (Infra lead), Cam (Retail ops lead)

High-level asks
- Replace legacy rule-based returns assistant with LLM-powered suggestion + link-to-docs. Must be behind VPC and no PII leaves their network.
- Latency target: p50 < 200ms for autocomplete-style suggestions, p95 < 600ms.
- Throughput: steady 6 QPS during business hours, burst to 25 QPS for promotions.
- Cost sensitivity: they expect to keep per-1000-turn costs below $0.40 (hosted) or target quantized private deploy to cut token cost ~65%.

Environment constraints / gotchas
- On-prem proxy for all egress (strict outbound allowlist). They'll only permit TLS to pre-authorized IPs and will route via an internal bastion — need IP allowlist for control plane callbacks.
- KMS: key material must be in their AWS KMS (no Redwood-managed keys for any PII flows). Ask: clarify if envelope encryption acceptable for non-PII telemetry.
- Database: return rules live in Postgres 12 on EC2; prefer inference to call a microservice for lookups instead of direct DB reads from model code. Keep network hop minimal.
- Regulatory: EU customers in their tenant; data residency request for EU-specific model endpoints.

Model / serving notes
- Suggested initial stack: hosted Redwood API using a small Llama-derivative for rank/suggestion (latency friendly) + dedicated/private deployment for any prompt-completion flows touching PII.
- Evaluate 8-bit quantized GGML variants on Dedicated hardware for cost check. Ask SRE to run perf bench with seq_len 128, batch sizes: 1, 4, 8 (simulate suggestion workload).
- Cache: strong opportunity to use prefix caching — many queries start with SKU-specific prefixes. Need to instrument hit rate quickly.

Security / compliance TODOs (action owners)
- [Raj] Confirm KMS policy: can Redwood integrate with their CMK via cross-account role? (JIRA-CLI-9142) — due 2026-02-25
- [Maya/Hiro] Draft minimal network diagram for control-plane callbacks and webhooks; include port/IPs required — share with Palisade infra by 2026-02-20 (blocked on IPs)
- [Leah] Negotiate trial terms for Dedicated 90-day pilot; include SLA for p95 latency and burst support — capture in pilot MOU

Operational playbook (sketch)
- Canary rollout: route 5% of traffic to Redwood suggestion model for first 2 weeks; observe CTR and false positives. If false positive rate > 8% revert.
- Fallbacks: primary->lighter model (low-cost) -> rule-based system. Automatic fallback on 503 or token budget exceed.
- Monitoring: per-route token-cost dashboard, p50/p95 latency, cache hit rate, model drift (random sample eval against golden prompts weekly).

Short-term next steps (this week)
- Internal: Hiro to spin up local perf harness and run 3 quick benches (seq128, batch 1/4/8) on the SMX cluster — post results to linked JIRA. (owner: Hiro, 48h)
- Internal: Maya to request Palisade's IP ranges and KMS ARN, and confirm whether any egress via on-prem proxy will rewrite TLS SNI. (owner: Maya, 24h)
- External: Setup follow-up technical deep-dive with Palisade infra (30–45m) next Tue — include SRE, Hiro, Raj. (owner: Leah to schedule)

Notes to self / rough hypotheses
- Hypothesis: If we can demonstrate p95 < 400ms on Dedicated with 8-bit quant, they will accept Private deployment with KMS cross-account rather than full on-prem.
- Risk: On-prem proxy rewriting SNI will break our control-plane webhook validation; likely require a static IP+TLS cert pinning workaround.
- Quick win: Implement a thin adapter microservice that proxies model calls and strips PII before leaving their VPC; easier than rearchitecting ingestion pipeline.

Prompt engineering snippets (for internal experiment)
- "You are an assistant that suggests return resolutions based on SKU metadata and policy. If PII appears in input, redact it and ask for confirmation. Provide top-3 suggestions with confidence scores."
- Example test prompt: "Customer wants refund for order #3421 (SKU: P-RED-100). Item damaged. Policy allows refund within 30 days." Expected: 3 suggestions, 1 recommended path with reason (policy match), 2 alternatives.

Open questions (for Palisade)
- Can we get an NDA addendum to allow Redwood SRE to access perf logs during pilot?
- Is anonymization at ingestion enough, or do they want full in-region-only processing for EU tenants?
- Do they have any hard token budget per month? (They mentioned conservative ops budget but unsure of exact limit)

Raw contact / scheduling
- Simone (CTO) simone@palisade-retail.com — prefers Thurs 9–11 PT for follow-ups
- Raj (Infra) raj@palisade-retail.com — owns KMS/comms questions

Revision history
- 2026-02-18: initial capture from intake call (Maya)
- 2026-02-19: added security TODOs after offline with Leah
- 2026-03-11: appended perf bench request and clarified latency targets (Hiro)

End of notebook.

-- quick checklist to convert into pilot proposal (for MOU):
- Define pilot scope + success metrics (CTR lift, false positive %)
- Confirm infra constraints (KMS ARN, IP allowlist, proxy behavior)
- Perf benchmark results (seq128, batch sizes)
- Cost projection for hosted vs dedicated vs private quantized
- Draft fallback policy and rollback triggers
